description: First-time input MMIO GPIO: APB4 slave, eight external pins, one level interrupt source and a three-bit special random input.

resets.release: RTL asserts reset asynchronously on negedge rst_ni; release must satisfy clk_i recovery/removal timing.

interrupts.hold: irq_o stays high while IRQ_STATUS[0] is set and IRQ_EN[0] is set; IRQ_STATUS latches on any change of the sampled pin vector.
interrupts.clear: Read DATA_IN (offset 0x08) or write DATA_IN to clear IRQ_STATUS[0].

port_actions.reason: Declared special input: the profile allows the environment to change the three pin-mode bits on every clock; the component XORs them into the sampled pin vector.

semantics: Register map and side effects were read from examples/soc_generation/rtl/novagpio.sv.
APB4 access attributes come from src/myfuzz/protocols/plugins/apb4.json.
pready_o is tied high and pslverr_o reports offsets outside the documented register map, so every APB transfer completes in one ACCESS cycle.

Optional register declarations added for the generated software phase: reset_value is the register's post-reset value (data_out_q, dir_q and irq_en_q reset to 0); writable_bits is the mask the RTL really stores, because the register is declared 32 bits wide while the RTL keeps only PINS=8 bits (DATA_OUT, DIR) or one bit (IRQ_EN); clears_register names the declared register whose value proves a read_clears access took effect (reading DATA_IN clears irq_stat_q, which IRQ_STATUS exposes). IRQ_STATUS declares side_effect none and carries no clears_register: novagpio.sv clears irq_stat_q only on a DATA_IN access (novagpio.sv:89 for a write, :93 for a read), so a read of IRQ_STATUS clears nothing and a read_clears declaration on it would have been false about the DUT. The clearing access is declared on DATA_IN, whose clears_register is IRQ_STATUS.
verified: Physical ports and widths come from verilator elaboration of the pinned novagpio.sv.
unknown: Electrical drive strength and bidirectional pin behaviour are out of the first-phase scope; out and dir are exported as separate unidirectional signals.
